replacement: Abstract. Healthcare data sharing increasingly requires authorisation decisions in which the patient, a guardian set G, the authorised doctor D and institutional authorities participate without belonging to a single administrative domain. This research proposes a trust-oriented authorisation framework in which patient consent is represented as an evaluable consent object C = (I, A, P, T, L, E) whose identity, authority, policy, temporal, lifecycle and evidence conditions are verified at the time of access, with decentralised identifiers and verifiable credentials establishing participants, a threshold N of guardian approvals establishing collective authorisation, and policy-aware and lifecycle-aware evaluation constraining every request. The framework is realised in the HALAH prototype deployed on the Ethereum Sepolia testnet and validated through scenario-based, negative and adversarial testing, while formal security assurance remains the focus of the next research stage. The report presents the systematic literature review, the research questions and objectives RO1 to RO6, the MVC-based architecture, the proposed solution and its live demonstration, and the plan for the subsequent stage.
